content_html:
The virtue of reading Surah Kahf on Friday is that the reader is given a light that shines between the two Fridays, in a hadith graded sahih (authentic) by al-Albani. Its time begins at sunset on Thursday and ends at sunset on Friday. In this article we set out the narrations on the subject and the grading of each, as given in the Dorar hadith encyclopedia, the difference between what is established and what is weak, the virtue of the first and last ten verses as protection from the Dajjal (the Antichrist), the four themes of the surah in brief, and a practical plan to read the whole surah in about half an hour.

What is the virtue of reading Surah Al-Kahf on Friday?

The virtue of reading Surah Al-Kahf on Friday is that Allah gives its reader a light that shines between the two Fridays, as in the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri narrated by al-Hakim and al-Bayhaqi and graded sahih by al-Albani. According to many scholars, its time runs from sunset on Thursday to sunset on Friday, and it takes about 20 to 30 minutes to read.

Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said:

«إِنَّ مَنْ قَرَأَ سُورَةَ الْكَهْفِ يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ أَضَاءَ لَهُ مِنَ النُّورِ مَا بَيْنَ الْجُمُعَتَيْنِ»

"Whoever reads Surah Al-Kahf on Friday, a light will shine for him between the two Fridays." (Narrated by al-Hakim and al-Bayhaqi; graded sahih by al-Albani in Sahih al-Jami' 6470 and Sahih at-Targhib 736)

As for this light, it was said to be an inner light that the reader finds in his heart and in his guidance throughout the week, and it was also said to be a light for him on the Day of Resurrection; there is no contradiction between the two. The point is that reading it is a weekly habit that links one Friday to the next, and Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (may Allah be pleased with him) himself kept to it.

How authentic are the hadiths on Surah Al-Kahf on Friday?

Many phrases about the virtue of Surah Al-Kahf circulate in messages, and not all of them are established. Here is a summary of the best-known narrations and their grading as presented by the Dorar hadith encyclopedia (Arabic):

WordingSourceGrading
"Whoever reads Surah Al-Kahf on Friday, a light will shine for him between the two Fridays"Al-Hakim and al-Bayhaqi, from Abu Sa'idGraded sahih by al-Albani (Sahih al-Jami' 6470)
"Whoever reads Surah Al-Kahf on the night of Friday, a light will shine for him between himself and the Ancient House (the Ka'bah)"Ad-Darimi and al-Bayhaqi, from Abu Sa'idGraded sahih by al-Albani (Sahih al-Jami' 6471)
"A light will rise for him from beneath his feet to the clouds of the sky... and he will be forgiven what is between the two Fridays"Reported from Ibn 'UmarIts chain has weakness, and it is not established from the Prophet ﷺ
"Whoever memorises ten verses from the beginning of Surah Al-Kahf will be protected from the Dajjal"Sahih Muslim 809, from Abu ad-Darda'Sahih

An important note: the hadith of Abu Sa'id was narrated as the Prophet's ﷺ words (marfu'), and also as the words of Abu Sa'id himself (mawquf), and some hadith scholars preferred the mawquf version. But scholars said that a Companion would not state a virtue like this from his own opinion, so it takes the ruling of the Prophet's words. That is why scholars, among them Imam ash-Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on him), recommended reading it on Friday. As for the addition "and he will be forgiven what is between the two Fridays", it is not established, so do not share it attributed to the Prophet ﷺ.

When is the time for reading Surah Al-Kahf on Friday?

The narrations come with the wording "on Friday" and "on the night of Friday", and scholars reconciled them by saying that what is meant is the day with its night. In the Islamic reckoning the night comes before its day, so the night of Friday begins at sunset on Thursday. That is why many scholars said its time runs from sunset on Thursday to sunset on Friday, as in IslamQA: when to read Surat al-Kahf on Friday, and al-Azhar's Global Fatwa Centre agreed. Shaykh Ibn Baz said that reading it at any time on Friday is good, early or late in the day.

TimeDoes it count for the virtue?
Thursday afternoon ('Asr), before MaghribNo, the night of Friday has not begun yet
From Maghrib on Thursday until Fajr (the night of Friday)Yes, according to those who combined the two narrations
From Fajr on Friday until just before MaghribYes, this is "Friday" without any disagreement
After Maghrib on FridayNo, the night of Saturday has begun; reading is still good, but this particular virtue is not gained

You do not have to read it in one sitting. If you read part of it on the night of Friday and finish it after Fajr or after the prayer, you have read it in its time. Nor does it have to be in the mosque or before the Jumu'ah prayer.

Keeping up this habit is easier when the mushaf (Quran copy) is in your pocket. In Rafiq Al-Taa, a free Islamic app with no ads (Arabic interface), coming soon to Google Play, you will find the complete Madinah mushaf (604 pages), working offline. Tap any verse to see its explanation from Tafsir as-Sa'di or at-Tafsir al-Muyassar, both built into the app. You can also log your reading in the daily "My good deeds" list to keep your streak going.

What is the virtue of the first and last ten verses of Surah Al-Kahf?

One of the greatest things narrated about Surah Al-Kahf is that it is a fortress against the trial of the Dajjal, the greatest trial on the face of the earth. Abu ad-Darda' (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said:

«مَنْ حَفِظَ عَشْرَ آيَاتٍ مِنْ أَوَّلِ سُورَةِ الْكَهْفِ عُصِمَ مِنَ الدَّجَّالِ»

"Whoever memorises ten verses from the beginning of Surah Al-Kahf will be protected from the Dajjal." (Muslim 809). In another narration in Muslim: «مِنْ آخِرِ الْكَهْفِ» "from the end of Al-Kahf".

In the long hadith of an-Nawwas ibn Sam'an about the Dajjal, the Prophet ﷺ said: «فَمَنْ أَدْرَكَهُ مِنْكُمْ فَلْيَقْرَأْ عَلَيْهِ فَوَاتِحَ سُورَةِ الْكَهْفِ» "Whoever of you meets him, let him recite against him the opening verses of Surah Al-Kahf." (Muslim 2937). That is why scholars advised memorising the first ten verses (1-10) and the last ten (101-110), combining both narrations, and whoever can memorise the whole surah has done better still.

Commentators on the hadith said, about the wisdom of this, that the beginning of the surah contains the story of the People of the Cave, whose faith Allah protected from the trial of a tyrant king, and it shows such wonders of Allah's power that whoever has memorised it will not be deceived by the extraordinary things the Dajjal brings. The surah opens with:

﴿الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَنزَلَ عَلَىٰ عَبْدِهِ الْكِتَابَ وَلَمْ يَجْعَل لَّهُ عِوَجًا﴾

"[All] praise is [due] to Allah, who has sent down upon His Servant [Muhammad ﷺ] the Book and has not made therein any deviance." (Surah Al-Kahf 18:1, translation: Sahih International)

And it closes with:

﴿قُلْ إِنَّمَا أَنَا بَشَرٌ مِّثْلُكُمْ يُوحَىٰ إِلَيَّ أَنَّمَا إِلَٰهُكُمْ إِلَٰهٌ وَاحِدٌ ۖ فَمَن كَانَ يَرْجُو لِقَاءَ رَبِّهِ فَلْيَعْمَلْ عَمَلًا صَالِحًا وَلَا يُشْرِكْ بِعِبَادَةِ رَبِّهِ أَحَدًا﴾

"Say, 'I am only a man like you, to whom has been revealed that your god is one God. So whoever would hope for the meeting with his Lord - let him do righteous work and not associate in the worship of his Lord anyone.'" (Surah Al-Kahf 18:110, translation: Sahih International)

This ending refutes the Dajjal's claim to divinity: the Messenger himself is a human being, and God is One with no partner.

What are the themes of Surah Al-Kahf? The four stories in brief

Surah Al-Kahf is a Makkan surah of 110 verses built around four stories. Many contemporary commentators see each one as addressing one of life's trials, and see the mention of protection from the Dajjal as fitting, since he brings all these trials together. This summary draws on reliable tafsir works such as Tafsir Ibn Kathir and Tafsir as-Sa'di:

StoryVerses (approx.)TrialThe way to safety
The People of the Cave9-26Trial of faithSteadfastness, righteous company and fleeing with one's faith
The owner of the two gardens32-44Trial of wealthGratitude, remembering the Hereafter and saying "Ma sha' Allah, la quwwata illa billah"
Musa and al-Khidr60-82Trial of knowledgeHumility, seeking knowledge and patience with what one does not fully grasp
Dhul-Qarnayn83-98Trial of power and authoritySincerity and attributing success to Allah: ﴿هَٰذَا رَحْمَةٌ مِّن رَّبِّي﴾ "This is a mercy from my Lord" (18:98, translation: Sahih International)

The People of the Cave: young men who believed in their Lord

Young men fled with their faith from a people who worshipped other than Allah. Allah sheltered them in a cave and made them sleep for many years, then raised them as a sign to people of His power to resurrect. Among its lessons: holding to the truth may cost a person what he loves, and Allah protects whoever protects his faith.

The owner of the two gardens: when wealth makes its owner forget

A man was given two great gardens. He was deceived by them, thought they would never perish and denied the Hour, so Allah destroyed his fruit and he was left wringing his hands in regret. The surah follows the story with: ﴿الْمَالُ وَالْبَنُونَ زِينَةُ الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا ۖ وَالْبَاقِيَاتُ الصَّالِحَاتُ خَيْرٌ عِندَ رَبِّكَ ثَوَابًا وَخَيْرٌ أَمَلًا﴾ "Wealth and children are [but] adornment of the worldly life. But the enduring good deeds are better to your Lord for reward and better for [one's] hope." (Surah Al-Kahf 18:46, translation: Sahih International)

Musa and al-Khidr: above every knower is One more knowing

Musa (peace be upon him) travelled in search of knowledge to a righteous servant whom Allah had given knowledge. He saw him do three things that looked wrong on the surface: damaging the boat, killing the boy and rebuilding the wall without payment. Then the hidden wisdom of each was explained to him. Among its lessons: human knowledge is limited, and behind Allah's decrees lie wisdoms that may be hidden from us.

Dhul-Qarnayn: power in the service of truth

A righteous king whom Allah established in the land. He reached the east and the west, established justice and built the barrier against Ya'juj and Ma'juj (Gog and Magog), then attributed all of it to his Lord's mercy, not to his own strength. Among its lessons: being given power is a trust.

If you want to go deeper into the meanings of the verses, read our article on the difference between Tafsir as-Sa'di and at-Tafsir al-Muyassar to choose the one that suits you.

How can you read Surah Al-Kahf in 20 to 30 minutes?

In the Madinah mushaf, Surah Al-Kahf runs from page 293 to page 304, that is, 12 pages. The sixteenth juz' (part) begins within it, at the verse: ﴿قَالَ أَلَمْ أَقُل لَّكَ إِنَّكَ لَن تَسْتَطِيعَ مَعِيَ صَبْرًا﴾ "[Al-Khidr] said, 'Did I not tell you that with me you would never be able to have patience?'" (Surah Al-Kahf 18:75, translation: Sahih International). An average reader reads a page in about two minutes, so the whole surah takes between 20 and 30 minutes depending on reading speed and tajweed. Here is a suggested plan if you cannot read it in one sitting:

SittingPagesSuggested timeApprox. duration
First293-295The night of Friday, after Maghrib or 'Isha6-8 minutes
Second296-298After Fajr on Friday6-8 minutes
Third299-301Before going to the Jumu'ah prayer6-8 minutes
Fourth302-304After 'Asr, before Maghrib6-8 minutes

Tips to help you keep it up every week:

  • Tie it to a fixed time: for example, always read it after Fajr on Friday; a habit linked to a set time is easier to keep.
  • Reflect on one story each week: read the whole surah, but pause at one story and read its tafsir, so you cover all four stories in a month.
  • Listen to a skilled reciter: listening is a good deed that helps you read correctly, but the virtue in the hadith is for the one who "reads", so make listening a help, not a replacement.
  • Memorise the first ten verses gradually: a verse or two each Friday, and you will have them in a month or two.
  • Do not make it a race: slow reading with correct tajweed is better than rushing; the aim is reflection, not just finishing.

If you read from your phone while travelling or somewhere without a connection, read our article on reading the Quran offline.

Can I read Surah Al-Kahf from my phone and without wudu?

Yes, you may read it from your phone, and you gain the virtue, in sha' Allah, because it is reading. As for wudu: reading the Quran from memory or from a phone while in a state of minor impurity is allowed by agreement of the scholars, and wudu is better and more complete. As for touching a paper mushaf, most scholars require purity for it, and many contemporary scholars do not give a phone the ruling of a mushaf. Someone in a state of major impurity has particular rulings, for which scholars should be consulted.

How do you make Surah Al-Kahf part of your Friday?

Reading Surah Al-Kahf is one of the Sunnahs of Friday, and it is good to combine it with the others in one routine: taking a bath (ghusl) and going early to the prayer, sending abundant blessings on the Prophet ﷺ, and seeking the hour of answered du'a. We have detailed these Sunnahs in our article on the Sunnahs of Friday, and explained the most likely times of the hour of answered du'a on Friday and how to make the most of it.

Summary

The virtue of reading Surah Al-Kahf on Friday is established by the hadith of Abu Sa'id graded sahih by al-Albani: a light between the two Fridays. Its time runs from sunset on Thursday to sunset on Friday, and it takes about half an hour, or four short sittings. Also try to memorise the first and last ten verses for protection from the Dajjal, as in Sahih Muslim, and reflect on its four stories, which address the trials of faith, wealth, knowledge and power. Do not share the weak additions attributed to the Prophet ﷺ. For questions about your own circumstances, it is best to ask scholars in your country.

faq.q: When does the time for reading Surah Kahf on Friday begin?
faq.a: According to many scholars it begins at sunset on Thursday, because the night of Friday starts at sunset, and it ends at sunset on Friday. The evidence is that the narrations came with both wordings, on Friday and on the night of Friday, so scholars reconciled them as the day with its night. You may split the reading over more than one sitting within this time.

faq.q: Is the hadith about Surah Kahf on Friday authentic?
faq.a: The hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, whoever reads Surah Al-Kahf on Friday, a light will shine for him between the two Fridays, was narrated by al-Hakim and al-Bayhaqi and graded sahih by al-Albani in Sahih al-Jami'. It was also narrated as Abu Sa'id's own words, and scholars said such a report takes the ruling of the Prophet's words. The addition about being forgiven between the two Fridays is not established.

faq.q: How many pages is Surah Kahf and how long does it take to read?
faq.a: In the Madinah mushaf, Surah Al-Kahf runs from page 293 to page 304, that is 12 pages, and it has 110 verses. An average reader reads a page in about two minutes, so the surah takes between 20 and 30 minutes depending on reading speed.

faq.q: Is listening to Surah Kahf on Friday enough?
faq.a: Listening to the Quran is a good deed with reward, but the hadith mentions the virtue for the one who reads Surah Al-Kahf, so many scholars hold that the specific virtue is gained by reading. It is better to read it yourself, and use listening to a skilled reciter to help you read correctly.

faq.q: Which verses of Surah Kahf protect from the Dajjal?
faq.a: Muslim narrated (809) from Abu ad-Darda' that whoever memorises ten verses from the beginning of Surah Al-Kahf will be protected from the Dajjal, and in another narration of his: from the end of Al-Kahf. So it is good to memorise verses 1 to 10 and verses 101 to 110, combining both narrations, and memorising the whole surah is better still.

faq.q: Can I read Surah Kahf from my phone without wudu?
faq.a: Yes. Reading the Quran from memory or from a phone while in a state of minor impurity is allowed, and wudu is better. Many contemporary scholars do not give a phone the ruling of a paper mushaf with regard to touching it. Someone in a state of major impurity has particular rulings, for which scholars should be consulted.

faq.q: If I missed Surah Kahf on Friday, can I read it on Saturday?
faq.a: Reading the Quran is good at any time, but the specific virtue in the hadith is tied to Friday and its night, so once the sun sets on Friday its time has passed. You can make a point of reading it earlier the next week, such as on the night of Friday or after Fajr, so you do not miss it.
